subject: CAIQ control mapping + sample artifacts — delivery & routing checklist
messages:
From: Evelyn Park <evelyn.park@helixbank.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@helixbank.com>, HelixBank Security <security@helixbank.com>
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: CAIQ control mapping + example artifacts for scoped endpoints

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking this on. As discussed with Carlos, the internal audit team needs a CAIQ mapping that ties Redwood's control statements to the CSA controls in our scoped environment (data-in-transit, key management, tenant isolation). To help our reviewers, can you provide: 

- A control crosswalk (CAIQ question -> Redwood assertion -> evidence pointer)
- One or two representative artifacts per critical control (e.g., proof of KMS rotation, sample runtime logs showing tenant separation)
- Brief notes where we have compensating controls or planned mitigations

Target is to ingest these into our assessment tracker by next Friday (2028-05-19). If any artifacts are sensitive, we can provision SFTP access; otherwise a Drive folder is fine.

Example ask: KMS rotation proof should include a rotation schedule entry + an exported key-change log showing the operation id and timestamp.

Can you confirm owners and a short delivery plan?

Appreciate it — Evelyn
HelixBank — Information Risk & Assurance

-----
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evelyn Park <evelyn.park@helixbank.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@helixbank.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: CAIQ control mapping + example artifacts for scoped endpoints

Evelyn — thanks for the clear list. Planned approach below; owners are tagged and timelines are conservative to allow legal/sensitivity review.

Plan (high level):
1) Crosswalk draft (CAIQ -> Redwood assertion -> artifact pointer) — owner: Kimberly Park — deliverable: RDW-CAIQ-mapping-draft.xlsx (shared link below). Target: 2028-05-14 EOD.
2) Artifact collection — owners: Jonas Weber (runtime logs, telemetry) and Priyom Das (crypto/key rotation artifacts). Target upload window: 2028-05-15 to 2028-05-17.
3) Sensitivity review & transfer instructions — owner: Marissa Cole (legal & secure transfer). If artifacts contain customer-identifiable data we will redact or provide redacted extracts.
4) Final delivery & intake to Helix tracker — Soojin to coordinate, target: 2028-05-18.

I’ve uploaded a working draft of the crosswalk and a short transfer checklist here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cDEf-exAMPLE (RDW-CAIQ-mapping-draft.xlsx).

Attachment plan: if Helix prefers DocuSign-protected transfer for a handful of signed attestations, Marissa will send a DocuSign envelope with the transfer agreement.

Open items for Helix:
- Preferred transfer channel (Drive link vs SFTP vs DocuSign package)?
- Any controls you want prioritized (e.g., KMS/key rotation, tenant isolation, KV cache retention)?

Kimberly, Jonas, Priyom — looping you in so owners see the deadlines and can flag any blockers.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Senior Security Programs Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: evidence-transfer-instructions.pdf (checklist)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: CAIQ control mapping + example artifacts for scoped endpoints

Got it — I’ll own the CAIQ crosswalk. Quick notes on artifacts I’ll attach to the workbook: 

- Control: KMS rotation (CSA SC-13 equivalent) — artifact: key-rotation-sample.txt (exported KMS change log, redacted key ids).
- Control: Tenant isolation (CSA NET-ISO) — artifact: runtime-tenant-segmentation-snippet.log (snippets showing tenant id and isolation headers).
- Control: Data-in-transit (CSA ENC-01) — artifact: tls-config-snippet.txt (ciphers, minimum TLS version) + a screenshot of load balancer TLS policy.

I’ll populate the RDW-CAIQ-mapping-draft.xlsx with one-line rationales and pointer links to the Drive folder. If anyone needs to flag that an artifact must be redacted, reply-all with the exact file name and reason.

Estimate: initial crosswalk populated by 2028-05-14 morning, artifacts uploaded by 2028-05-16.

—Kimberly
Director, Security Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Evelyn Park <evelyn.park@helixbank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 13 May 2028 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: CAIQ control mapping + example artifacts for scoped endpoints

Evelyn — we can do DocuSign for the transfer agreement (covers handling of PII and retention limits). I have prepared a short transfer checklist and the envelope is ready pending your signatory. DocuSign envelope: DocuSign://envelope/0a1b2c3d4e

If Helix signs the envelope, we will:
- Provision a read-only Drive folder (no public links) and drop the requested artifacts there.
- Add file-level redaction as needed before upload; if an artifact cannot be redacted we will provide a sampling extract and a certified attestation.
- Share a short manifest (RDW-artifact-manifest.csv) that lists artifact, owner, sensitivity, and redaction status.

Next steps for Helix: sign the DocuSign envelope OR confirm SFTP details if you prefer an alternate transfer method.

Thanks — I’ll be on standby to expedite when sign-off is complete.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Security Operations Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: evidence-transfer-instructions.pdf
